title: One-loop pure-scalar MSbar closure and polynomial RG check
scope: Four real scalars phi,x,y,D, X=(x+i*y)/sqrt(2), original Candidate 1 matching. No Standard Model, gravitational, thermal, finite-density or derivative corrections are calculated.
notation: mp,mx,md are signed mass-squared coefficients, not masses; B_z=16*pi^2*d z/d ln(mu).
quartic_tensor: V4=lambda_abcd z_a z_b z_c z_d/4!. Explicit seed tensors with all permutations: 0000=6lp,1111=2222=6lx,3333=6ld,0011=0022=2c,0033=2d,1122=2lx,1133=2233=2alpha.
tensor_beta: B_lambda_abcd=sum_ef(lambda_abef*lambda_efcd+lambda_acef*lambda_efbd+lambda_adef*lambda_efbc); B_m_ab=sum_cd(lambda_abcd*m_cd); B_C=Tr((m^2)^2)/2. Scalar gamma=0 at this loop order.
independent_route: Construct V0 directly as a polynomial; differentiate twice to obtain its field Hessian H=M^2; compare every exact coefficient of sum_z B_z*dV0/dz and Tr(H*H)/2.
arithmetic: Python standard-library Fraction coefficients in a sparse multivariate polynomial implementation; no symbolic package installation or floating-point cancellation is used for identity checks.
checks: All 256 quartic tensor components remain in the declared coupling family
Mass tensor remains diagonal with equal x/y entries
Derived projected betas equal the stated candidate formulas coefficient-by-coefficient
Full independent polynomial RG identity including the constant term
Display nonzero RG residuals if generated alpha, mX2, or vacuum C beta is incorrectly omitted
numeric_output: Evaluate exact beta numerators and beta values at matching. Show only first-order leading-log parameter changes at mu/mu0=1/2,1,2; no coupling search or fit.
vacuum_energy: Distinguish polynomial C, tree minimum value C-mp^2/(4lp), scalar one-loop vacuum value, and separately matched total gravitational rho_Lambda. Do not impose tree C=lp*v^4/4 as an RG-invariant identity without checking it.
limits: The constant-background CW potential is a zero-derivative diagnostic, not the one-loop determinant or fixed-Q energy of a rotating inhomogeneous soliton; no pole mass, quantum stability or lifetime is calculated.
source: Stephen P. Martin, hep-ph/0111209v2, https://arxiv.org/html/hep-ph/0111209v2 , especially scalar one-loop potential and RG invariance conventions.
